jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Off the Record
jokes.joke: I married a journalist, so every argument has ground rules. I say, “Off the record,” and she says the rules changed—that only works before I say something stupid. Apparently “off the record” isn’t a time machine; it’s a tiny umbrella you open after the piano lands.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: House Rules
jokes.joke: My family has a strict living room rule: no phones during movie night. Been that way for years. Then last week I caught my dad on his phone, and instead of getting mad, I just said, 'New rule — no phones.' He goes, 'Since when?' I said, 'Since you got caught. That's how rules work in this house. They're not laws, they're reactions.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Active Listening
jokes.joke: I realized I’m way too empathetic to be an ER doctor. A guy comes in with a severed finger, screaming in agony, so I immediately start screaming too. I’m like, 'I feel you, man! This is so unfair! We're both having a terrible Tuesday!' The nurses are yelling at me to apply pressure, and I'm just holding his good hand, sobbing, 'Your feelings are perfectly valid!' Turns out, massive blood loss requires medical intervention, not active listening.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Badge of Courage
jokes.joke: I'm an emergency room physician, but between us, I'm a total coward. Last night a guy rolls in with a steak knife still stuck in his chest, and my medical training kicks in perfectly—I scream louder than he does, point at the exit signs, and hide under a gurney until the real doctors show up.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Living Room Panic
jokes.joke: I found out I’m a complete coward when a bird flew into my living room. I didn’t try to guide it out—I just grabbed my coat and left like it had legally claimed the space. I even texted my friend, “If you hear chirping, that’s the new tenant. I’m not going back in there.”
